scope: Proposition 4.4 (Functorial good-reduction comparison) of the manuscript “Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold” (preprints/Quaternionic-Division-Points-on-Curves-in-the-Siegel-Threefold-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e11b4b068502ced9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At a finite place, suppose a point t is on a sufficiently small actual center branch. After coefficient extension the two polarized abelian schemes have a common special fiber A. More precisely, over a finite local extension F with residue field k, put F0 = W(k)[1/p] and D = H1 cris(A/W(k))[1/p]. There are rational comparison isomorphisms cu : H1 dR(Au/F) −→ D ⊗F0 F, u = t0, t, whose transition c−1 t0 ct is horizontal transport. They are compatible with morphisms of either lifted fiber and their specializations, including morphisms which do not extend over the base curve. Ramification of the coefficient field is allowed. In particular, if βi and αj are the specializations of the centered and target endomorphisms, then ⟨Bi, Y (a)Pj⟩ = 1 4 Tr(βiαj) ∈ Q (1 ≤ i, j ≤ 2). (4.5) The cross pairings belong to 1 4Z, and their ordinary absolute values are at most C(dh)c. At archimedean places the same assertions hold with integral Betti transport in place of specialization.
